title: IA-MNS Implementation Plan
html:
Project human actions · Project derivation · Validation · Documentation index

Purpose and baseline

This is IA-MNS's living execution plan and the current plan for this repository. It tracks product and repository work; the README, current policies, and accepted ADRs govern implementation.

IA-MNS was initialized on 2026-10-01 from Orion commit 53bcc705a9f68f01aa1bbea3a0f4df4a009577ea of https://github.com/GabriellMDias/Orion. The project manifest records that immutable initialization commit and the Orion baseline currently integrated. The repository starts with the foundation's architecture, policies, ADRs, tooling, validation gate, CI, generated references, and Living Documentation Portal, and with no product modules. Results recorded for the Orion repository are not results for this repository until they pass in this checkout and in this repository's CI.

Maintaining this plan

Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain this plan and the project human actions within the user's authorized scope.

  1. Before implementation, inspect actual repository state, the relevant task, its prerequisites, governing policy, and linked human actions. Do not treat a planned capability or unchecked action as available.
  2. Mark a task in progress when work actually starts. Update statuses when evidence, scope, dependencies, or blockers change, and before each handoff or completion report.
  3. Allocate stable task IDs as PJ-NN; never reuse or renumber them. Add finer tasks when needed; do not hide unfinished subtasks inside a completed row.
  4. Record concise evidence in the task row: implementation paths, validation commands and results, review references, or a linked decision. Record evidence produced for this repository—local validation, this repository's CI runs, and this repository's external settings. Do not store secret values or sensitive output.
  5. A task becomes completed only when its deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence. A partial implementation or an unavailable required check is not completion.
  6. When human intervention is necessary, add or update a project human action, link it from the affected task, mark that task blocked, and tell the user what is needed. Continue independent authorized work where possible.
  7. A future prerequisite is pending, not automatically blocked.
  8. When scope or sequencing changes, use changed, explain why and what replaces the work, and link supporting decisions. Do not delete unresolved obligations to make the plan look complete.
  9. Update command availability, current documentation, generated artifacts, and the human actions in the same coherent change where applicable. Do not change ADR status merely to record implementation progress.
Status Meaning
pending Not started; includes conditional work whose trigger has not occurred.
in progress Work has started and is incomplete.
completed Applicable deliverables and acceptance criteria are satisfied with evidence.
blocked The identified work cannot proceed without a recorded dependency, decision, access, or correction.
changed Scope, applicability, or sequencing was explicitly revised; reason and replacement or disposition are recorded.

Constraints throughout implementation

  • Retain the accepted stack recorded in the technology map; incompatibilities require explicit resolution rather than silent substitution.
  • Add product capabilities as API modules and web modules composed in apps/api/src/modules.ts and apps/web/src/modules.tsx; Orion's reference implementation shows a complete example.
  • Deliver tests, security controls, telemetry, and documentation with the behavior they protect.
  • Keep generated artifacts reproducible and subordinate to canonical sources. Reviewed SQL migrations follow their separate release-history rules.
  • Require non-mutating pnpm validate for substantial changes, using the same capabilities locally and in CI.
  • Adopt newer Orion revisions only through the reviewed upgrade workflow.

Current work

Task Scope Status Evidence / dependency

No application table or ERP migration is needed. completed API module, sales result renderer, decision, generated API/SDK/portal. Local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-01, including 18 browser journeys. Provider boundary tests use synthetic data; live acceptance remains PJ-06.
PJ-06 Configure dedicated external providers and reconcile live Portuguese questions and Oracle 12.1 totals against the owner's reference. blocked On 2026-10-01, nine structured queries and the complete current-period reference projection matched real Oracle 12.1.0.2 data using isolated Client 19.32. Actual HTTP/Oracle comparison and empty-result checks passed with a controlled planner. Description matching, query budgets, comparison products, formatting, and malformed provider results were hardened. Live evidence and limits. The owner subsequently provisioned a key manually and authorized reuse; PH-07 is complete. Ten actual language requests, eight direct original-SQL reconciliations, and real-browser acceptance passed; live verification. PH-08 now retains only weight/currency confirmation; PJ-41 completed the dedicated Runtime access.
PJ-07 Audit the complete sales MVP for internal-pilot readiness, correct relevant defects, review desktop/mobile presentation, and rerun Orion's full gate without adding domains. completed Readiness audit, 2026-10-01: model clarification text removed; socket budgets, comparison boundaries, bounded monthly filling, Oracle response scope, and previous-only/negative result presentation corrected. Actual HTTP with real Oracle passed comparison, no-result, and 311-row product detail using a controlled planner. Desktop/mobile synthetic journeys and accessibility passed. Frozen installation and full pnpm validate passed: 82 API tests, 63 web unit tests, 5 browser tests, 19 end-to-end journeys. Subsequent PJ-08 verified live interpretation and browser behavior with the owner-authorized key; shared rollout remains dependent on PH-08 and PJ-05.
PJ-08 Diagnose the reported live sales runtime failure, validate existing OpenAI credentials and Oracle separately, then reconcile live natural-language sales queries. completed Live verification, 2026-10-01: supplied runtime event confirmed DPI-1047 during native client loading; fresh Thin reproduced NJS-116. Compatible Client 19.32 and a complete watcher restart restored the runtime. Existing key/model and Oracle were separately validated. Ten real HTTP scenarios passed; eight numerical answers matched the original SQL, and the real browser question/reconciliation/context deletion passed. Internal diagnostics now identify provider/stage, with redaction regressions. Frozen installation and full pnpm validate passed: 86 API tests, 63 web unit tests, 5 browser tests, 19 end-to-end journeys. PH-07 is complete; PH-08 still requires a dedicated SELECT-only account and unit confirmations.
PJ-09 Evolve IA-MNS into the corporate agent: implemented-capability catalog, grounded conversation, actual execution progress, light/dark themes, local Docker PostgreSQL and durable actor-owned conversation/context. Preserve the sales capability and run Orion gates. completed Architecture, ADR-0019, verification, 2026-10-01: implemented and locally provisioned. Fourteen real HTTP scenarios and eight original-SQL reconciliations passed; actual PostgreSQL/API restart recovery and real-browser context continuation passed. Frozen installation and complete local pnpm validate passed: 92 API, 63 web unit, five browser component tests and 20 end-to-end journeys. Shared lifecycle/release controls remain conditional PH-09/PH-10; PH-08 remains unchanged.
PJ-10 Enable temporary owner-controlled phone testing on a selected LAN interface without exposing credential-free developer access, databases or production authentication. completed ADR-0020, procedure, 2026-10-01: separate private-interface web/loopback API, expiring bearer and HTTP Web Crypto UUID fallback implemented. Actual LAN-origin mobile-viewport browser passed social chat, real OpenAI/Oracle monthly apple sales and persisted history recovery; missing/incorrect bearer and foreign origin rejected. Duplicate launch preserves the active credential; credential files and logs remain protected. Existing Node firewall rules needed no change. Complete local pnpm validate passed: 94 API, 63 web unit, five browser component tests and 20 end-to-end journeys. Physical phone reachability still needs the owner's device test; router/client isolation was not verified from that device.
PJ-11 Give the corporate agent a full-window conversation layout with a collapsible desktop sidebar, modal mobile history, and compact light/dark presentation. completed Presentation, 2026-10-01: removed outer card/margins and duplicate product header; neutral light/dark workspace, 260-pixel collapsible desktop history, native mobile modal and bottom composer implemented. Synthetic browser checks and visual review covered 1366×768/1024×600 notebooks and 390×844/320×568 mobile viewports, accessible themes/modal keyboard recovery, full available width and retained conversation state. Actual local runtime reopened/reloaded an existing monthly result and exercised sidebar/mobile controls without new provider requests. Complete local pnpm validate passed: 94 API, 63 web unit, five browser component tests and 21 end-to-end journeys.
PJ-04 Replace the neutral placeholder brand mark and touch icon with the product's visual identity. completed IA-MNS monogram in canonical SVG; touch icon regenerated with pnpm -C apps/web identity:write. Desktop/mobile chat preview reviewed on 2026-10-01.
PJ-12 Restore the original shared product/documentation colors while preserving PJ-11's full-window layout and collapsible history. completed Owner clarification of 2026-10-02: removed only the workspace's neutral palette overrides, reusing the existing light/dark tokens in styles.css. Existing theme/persistence/accessibility browser journey passed across desktop/mobile and documentation; restored colors were visually reviewed and stylesheet formatting passed. PJ-11's layout and behavior remain unchanged.
PJ-13 Animate and resize the sidebar, retain a collapsed icon rail, and persist per-conversation organization/search while preserving palettes and sales behavior. completed Verification, 2026-10-02: owner-scoped rename/pin/archive/restore/search, additive local migration, native menus/modals, pointer/keyboard resize and reduced-motion transitions implemented. Actual local HTTP/PostgreSQL reconnect verified metadata, search, restore/delete and preserved existing history count without provider calls. Complete local pnpm validate passed: 95 API tests, 63 web unit tests, five browser component tests and 23 end-to-end journeys. Generated API/SDK/schema/portal and lifecycle documentation updated. No new human blocker.
PJ-14 Reconcile the plan, human actions, and documentation with the verified repository settings, apply the owner's Apache-2.0 license decision, and open the first pull request with all work developed so far. completed 2026-10-03: verified publication, the main ruleset, Renovate, and GitHub security settings through the GitHub API; PH-01, PH-03, and PH-06 are complete. ADR-0021 records the license. PH-02 and PH-04 still need evidence from the first pull request run: the required gate and dependency review. Merging stays with the owner. Completed 2026-10-04: pull request #2 passed Dependency review and Orion required gate (run 37156241037) and the owner merged it with merge commit 689e728; PH-02 and PH-04 are complete.
PJ-15 Implement the IA-MNS identity: Person, local accounts with TOTP and recovery, PDT Connect and Sankhya links, provisioning, linking/unlinking, sessions and the access-token issuer, permission catalog with provider policy, principal administrator and bootstrap, one frontend for direct and embedded surfaces, and a Sankhya connector independent of the login mechanism. completed 2026-10-04: identity domain, ADR-0022, ADR-0023; API module features/identity, additive migration 202610040001_identity, web features/identity, embedded basepath and frame policy. Frozen installation and the complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-04: 109 API tests (14 identity tests, including two full scenarios on migrated PostgreSQL), 63 web unit tests, five browser component tests and 27 end-to-end journeys (4 identity journeys: bootstrap with TOTP, embedded PDT with silent re-handshake and no cookies, direct PDT and local MFA sign-in reaching the same Person, hostile framing blocked), plus format, lint, types, architecture, documentation, references, builds and smoke. Remote CI is reported by the pull request. Real PDT homologation (PJ-16) and the Om add-on (PJ-17) remain human-blocked; no production identity is deployed.
PJ-16 Validate the PDT Connect direct and embedded sign-in against an HTTPS homologation installation with the real contract. blocked PH-12: homologation URL, client registration and PDT host page. The connector and bridge pass synthetic contract tests and browser journeys. On 2026-10-06 the PDT host screen was implemented in the PDT Connect repository and the embedded flow passed against a local PDT (PJ-27); the HTTPS homologation remains.
PJ-17 Publish the reviewed Sankhya Om add-on to the production Om and approve Om-session sign-in for production. blocked PH-11 (Om HTTPS, session cookie, redirects, direct HTTP exposure) and PH-14 (production key custody and publication); depends on PJ-24. The IA-MNS verifier, flows and production gate (SANKHYA_SESSION_TRUST) are implemented and tested; the legacy credential login remains an unimplemented fallback. On 2026-10-06 the scope was narrowed: ADR-0026 fixed the packaging, and developing and validating the add-on in the development environment moved to PJ-24.
PJ-18 Correct the user-creation model: no public self-registration; automatic first access through Sankhya or PDT Connect; no duplicate Person and no linking by weak evidence (e-mail is a hint that asks for proof); proof-based and owner consolidation; owner creation with a directory-selected Sankhya user, proof-based link invitations and an optional local invitation. completed 2026-10-05: identity domain, amended (unpublished) ADR-0022. Local validation: every pnpm validate step through the production builds passed (110 API tests including the identity journeys on migrated PostgreSQL, 63 web unit and five browser component tests); the API smoke first exceeded its 5-second exit limit while the machine was under external load and passed on rerun; the 27 end-to-end journeys then passed separately. The Sankhya directory needs the reader view in PH-08; real PDT and Om proofs remain PJ-16/PJ-17.
PJ-19 Require sign-in for product screens on the direct surface, redesign the sign-in and invitation screens, and replace the sidebar's account links with an avatar-and-name account menu. completed 2026-10-05: web guide, identity domain. Local checks passed: lint, types, 63 web unit and five browser component tests, production build and bundle check, and all 27 end-to-end journeys (direct access redirects to /entrar; the account menu lists its entries, takes focus and closes with Escape; embedded menus offer no sign-out; environments without identity keep the plain sidebar).
PJ-20 Evolve the AI architecture for reliable, extensible and measurable analytics: structured conversation state with pending requests, an analytical plan between interpretation and execution, a structured-model port, explicit AI tracing, and an evaluation framework with curated regression datasets, live-model runs, trace capture, synthetic candidates and simulation. Resolve the reported loss of a pending sales request after a period-only answer without a prompt-specific workaround. No new ERP semantics, providers, fine-tuning or self-modifying behavior. completed Owner request of 2026-10-05; ADR-0024, AI interpretation, AI evaluation. Sales context version 2, deterministic relation normalization, filter grounding, application-resolved periods, catalog-derived interpretation schema, pending-request routing, src/ai/ model port, IA_MNS_AI_TRACE with additive migration 202610050001_agent_turn_traces, and apps/api/evals/ with 39 curated cases. Complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-05: 218 API tests (including every curated case replayed, framework tests and content traces on migrated PostgreSQL), 63 web unit tests, five browser component tests and 27 end-to-end journeys, plus every static, reference and build check. Opt-in live runs with the owner-authorized key and model gpt-6.1-sol, synthetic text only: the first run passed 35/38 cases; it exposed a missing rule for context-dependent follow-ups (fixed in interpreter version 2026-10-05.2), one forecast case with a wrong expectation (reworded and split into period/future-month-asks-again and unsupported/sales-forecast) and transient provider errors (503/timeouts, now retried by evaluation only). The final run passed 39/39 cases and 60/60 turns with clarification precision and recall of 100%, no unintended constraints, p50 turn latency 10.8 s and p95 13.7 s. Goal simulation reached 5 of 5 conclusive goals (one inconclusive provider outage); a synthetic generation proposed four candidates whose plural product expectations contradicted the documented rule, confirming they need review. The new migration was not applied to the owner's local volume.
PJ-21 Make the authentication policy administrable: session duration, inactivity, recent-authentication windows, second-factor requirement and remembered browsers, with secure defaults, hard limits, explicit acknowledgement of reduced security, audit and fixed production safeguards; remove unexpected sign-outs caused by concurrent session renewals and make inactivity follow user activity. completed 2026-10-05: ADR-0025, identity domain, additive migration 202610050002_identity_security_policy. The complete local pnpm validate passed (224 API tests including three identity journeys on migrated PostgreSQL, 63 web unit and five browser component tests, 27 end-to-end journeys, smoke, builds, references and documentation); the later refinements (second-factor enrollment after invitations; owners may be remembered only under a non-production optional policy) were rechecked with the identity suites, lint, types, builds and the identity journeys. Production values remain an owner review under PH-15.
PJ-22 Adopt an MNS-derived visual identity: brand and interface palettes for the light and dark themes, a new IA-MNS symbol with a small-size favicon variant and horizontal lockups, their placement in the product and documentation portal, and a visual identity document. completed Owner request of 2026-10-05 with the MNS corporate logo as reference. Visual identity owns the palette, logos and usage rules; tokens in apps/web/src/styles.css, symbol, favicon and lockups in apps/web/src/assets, touch icon regenerated with pnpm -C apps/web identity:write. Every documented text pair meets WCAG AA in both themes; sign-in, documentation and synthetic chat screens were reviewed in light and dark at desktop and 390-pixel mobile widths. Complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-05: 225 API, 63 web unit, five browser component tests and 27 end-to-end journeys, smoke, builds, references and documentation.
PJ-23 Record the owner's Sankhya integration decisions and represent the official add-on template placed in apps/sankhya-addon in the architecture, repository tooling scope and documentation, without implementing add-on behavior or changing the template's build. completed 2026-10-06: ADR-0026 (Add-on Studio add-on, not a BI component, kept in this repository as a thin host; partly supersedes ADR-0023); application boundaries, identity, add-on guide and local instructions. The template guide was kept verbatim as apps/sankhya-addon/SANKHYA-TEMPLATE.md; no other template file changed. Prettier, ESLint and the documentation check now exclude the Gradle project and the Sankhya-supplied text, which had made them fail. PH-16 records the prepared development environment; PH-17 the open redistribution question. The Gradle build was not run, because the template's build was not changed. Local docs:check, format:check, lint, agents:check, docs:references:write/check/test and the complete pnpm validate ran on 2026-10-06: every step through the documentation references passed; one API test failed because a random request ID in the logs contained the digits it asserts are absent, and the rerun of pnpm test, build, smoke and test:e2e passed (225 API, 63 web unit, five browser component tests, 27 end-to-end journeys).
PJ-24 Develop and validate the Sankhya Om add-on in the prepared Sankhya development environment, before any production publication: replace the template examples with the menu screen that frames /embed/sankhya, the bridge answer and the assertion service signing with a development key; keep the appKey and private keys out of tracked files; settle the Gradle wrapper, line endings and dependency-update handling of the Gradle project. With a local IA-MNS, verify that a development Sankhya user opens IA-MNS without an IA-MNS sign-in, is provisioned with a link at first access and reaches the same Person afterwards, and that signed-out users, replayed or foreign-nonce assertions and other origins are refused. completed 2026-10-06: add-on IaMnsHostSP (ES256, 60 s, CODUSU from the Om session, CODUSU 0 refused, POST from the configured Om origin with X-IA-MNS-Host), host screen IaMns and the only Om artifact, its menu entry; template examples, guide, icon and parameters removed; appKey and WildFly folder in the ignored local.properties; official Gradle 8.2 wrapper with distribution checksum; plugin pinned to 2.20.1 without mavenLocal(); CRLF for gradlew.bat. pnpm sankhya:local provisions the development key and both sides' configuration outside the repository. In the development Om, with the real signed-in user VENDEDOR (CODUSU 3): the menu opened the official frontend without an IA-MNS sign-in, the first access provisioned the Person and its proof link automatically (person.provisioned), a conversation with the real agent succeeded, and reloading and reopening the Om reached the same Person and history. Refusals observed: SUP (no_authenticated_user), no Om session (Om login redirect or error, no assertion), missing host header (host_forbidden_origin), invalid nonce (host_invalid_request); real assertions replayed in the same flow (IDENTITY_FLOW_EXPIRED), used in another flow (nonce_mismatch), tampered or expired (invalid_assertion). The test exposed an IA-MNS web defect: a refused embedded handshake restarted itself endlessly through the identity status refetch; fixed in session.tsx with an end-to-end regression test that failed before the fix (132 attempts) and passes after it. ./gradlew model:test passed (8 tests). Linking an account already linked to another Person was covered by the existing automated identity tests, not reproduced in the Om (it needs a second signed-in Person). Validation results: VALIDATION_PLACEHOLDER. The direct-URL authorize page moved to PJ-25; committing template-derived files still waits for PH-17.
PJ-25 Add the direct-URL "Entrar com Sankhya" authorize page to the add-on and validate it against IA-MNS over HTTPS (its browser-binding cookie is SameSite=None; Secure). pending Split from PJ-24 on 2026-10-06. Needs an HTTPS development setup for the Om and IA-MNS; the embedded surface does not depend on it.
PJ-26 Apply the owner's requests of 2026-10-06: accept the shared SUP account (CODUSU 0) from the Om so it can be consolidated into the principal administrator's Person; trust only the Om HTTPS name in production and guide people who open the Om through another address; make light the default theme; offer "Entrar com Sankhya" on the direct URL only when its authorize page exists. in progress Verifier and add-on accept CODUSU 0 (unit tests); configuracao returns only the configured Om origin to other addresses and the screen points to it; assertion keeps the single trusted origin; light default with an end-to-end check under a dark OS preference; directSignInAvailable drives the direct methods and linkable providers, with a unit test and regenerated OpenAPI/SDK. In the development Om, SUP signed in and was provisioned automatically, and the owner gave that Person the owner role. On 2026-10-06 the owner removed that Person's owner role and consolidated it into the principal administrator (person.merged); the administrator now holds the sankhya:0 link and SUP opens the administrator's profile from the Om. Remaining check: observing the wrong-address guidance in the Om (opening it through an address other than the configured origin); it was not exercised. Production details stay outside this public repository (PH-11, PH-14). Complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-06 after these changes: 227 API, 63 web unit and five browser component tests, 28 end-to-end journeys, smoke, builds, references and documentation.
PJ-27 Provide the IA-MNS screen in PDT Connect, following PDT patterns (menu route, permission, parameters, migration and seed), so that a signed-in PDT user opens the official IA-MNS frontend inside the PDT without another sign-in, and validate it against a local PDT Connect with real PDT sign-in. Keep IA-MNS behavior in IA-MNS. completed 2026-10-06, owner request; changes in the PDT Connect repository (working tree, not committed): Nest module ia-mns with GET /api/ia-mns/host (JWT, ia-mns:acessar, validated against PDT_IDENTITY_CLIENTS), IntegrationClientService.isRegistered, migration 20261006120000_ia_mns_host and seed for the permission and the IA_MNS_URL, IA_MNS_CLIENT_ID and IA_MNS_REDIRECT_URI parameters, web screen /ia-mns with bridge v1 over the existing authorize endpoint, PDT guide section. PDT checks: Jest 22 tests (new service and client tests), browser test test:ia-mns, web and API typecheck and lint of the changed files. IA-MNS: pnpm pdt:local and directSignInAvailable for PDT (direct sign-in only with a callback on the IA-MNS origin, unit test). Real run with a local PDT (API on a database copy without schedules, PDTCONNECT_BOOTSTRAP=false): the unconfigured screen refused safely; after the administrator set the parameters, PDT user 0 opened IA-MNS without a sign-in, the Person and its proof link were provisioned automatically, a conversation worked (no business capability, as PDT links grant none), and reloading reached the same Person and history. Refused: reused code in its flow (IDENTITY_FLOW_EXPIRED), code in another flow and expired code (code_rejected), other issuer (issuer_mismatch), invalid PDT session (401, pdt_login_required), unregistered callback (400). With the screen open, the embedded session renewed silently for the same Person after its 10-minute token. Not exercised: a PDT user without ia-mns:acessar (guard-covered). PDT build of the web passed, and its identity suites passed (67 Jest tests, PGlite migration test, both browser tests). Complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-06 after these changes: 227 API, 63 web unit and five browser component tests, 28 end-to-end journeys, smoke, builds, references and documentation. HTTPS homologation and production remain PH-12.
PJ-28 Add VRMaster (PostgreSQL) as a second read-only sales source of the sales capability with the owner's reference SQL. The person chooses the source in an interface selector (MNS (Sankhya), Pilar da Terra (VR Master), Tudo), which replaced the earlier decision to ask which system; Tudo shows each source separately and never sums them. Same guarantees as Sankhya: fixed parameterized SQL, read-only transaction, bounded work, deterministic answers, no ERP writes. completed 2026-10-07: owner decisions and ADR-0027; sources and VRMaster semantics. The conversational "Sankhya or VRMaster?" question of 2026-10-06 was never implemented and is withdrawn. Reference SQL (PH-18) transcribed with every join in vrmaster-query.ts; node-postgres adapter vrmaster.ts (REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY, rolled back, 30-second statements, 5-second locks, cancellation by ending the connection); source-neutral SalesReader port with shared product-phrase matching; SalesChat runs the selected sources (parallel for Tudo, per-source failure, weight unavailable in VRMaster, notice when the text names another source); turn source with additive migration 202610070001_agent_turn_source, stored reply version 2 with read upgrade of version 1; interpreter sales-interpreter/2026-10-07.1; web Fonte selector in memory and per-source answers; settings VRMASTER_DB_* (PH-19). Tests: source routing, Tudo without sums, partial failures, selector changes, text that names another source, a source name dropped from the product filter, unavailable or unconfigured VRMaster and VRMaster weight (sales-sources.test.ts); the fixed SQL on PostgreSQL 16 with a synthetic VRMaster schema and the PH-19 grants (sales-vrmaster.test.ts); turn source persistence, replay conflict and version 1 upgrade on migrated PostgreSQL; six curated source evaluation cases; browser tests of the per-source answer; an end-to-end selector journey on a 375-pixel screen with keyboard selection and accessibility checks. Complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-07: 259 API tests, 63 web unit and seven browser component tests, smoke and 29 end-to-end journeys, plus every static, reference, documentation and build check. A live run with gpt-6.1-sol passed all 45 curated cases (67 turns). The development database received the migration. Reconciliation against the real VRMaster is PJ-29.
PJ-29 Connect IA-MNS to the real VRMaster with the PH-19 account and reconcile the VRMaster source with the owner's reference SQL before relying on its figures; decide the connection's protection in transit. blocked Split from PJ-28 on 2026-10-07. Blocked by PH-20 (the owner configures VRMASTER_DB_* and runs the reconciliation queries; IA-MNS has never connected to the real VRMaster) and, before shared or production use, PH-21 (the VRMaster server offers no TLS).
PJ-30 Make IA-MNS follow the light/dark theme selected in PDT Connect when opened inside it. completed 2026-10-07, owner request. Host bridge message ia-mns:host-theme and the initial ?theme= of the PDT embed URL (identity); the frame applies it only after the handshake confirms the PDT origin, hides its theme control there and stores nothing. PDT Connect repository (working tree): the IA-MNS screen sends the theme on load and on every change, with its browser test extended. Checks: web typecheck, the identity end-to-end journeys (embedded PDT theme, change by message, invalid value ignored, no control, nothing stored) and the PDT browser test. The run exposed an existing defect: saving the authentication policy remounted its form and could drop the "Política salva" confirmation; the confirmation now lives in the panel. Complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-07: 259 API, 63 web unit and seven browser component tests, smoke and 29 end-to-end journeys. Verified live with the local PDT: IA-MNS opened dark with the PDT dark theme and switched to light with the PDT switch, without reloading.
PJ-31 Make operational settings administrable: classify every API environment variable (secret, bootstrap, operational parameter default, development), turn the AI model, AI trace level and automatic grants by provider link into typed operational parameters persisted in the application database, and administer them in Administração → Parâmetros for the principal administrator only, with validation, concurrency protection, audit and effect without restart. completed 2026-10-08, owner request. ADR-0028, configuration policy, identity domain; catalog apps/api/src/parameters.ts, additive migration 202610080001_operational_parameters, web features/identity/parameters.tsx. The complete local pnpm validate passed on 2026-10-08: 269 API tests (catalog precedence, validation, production limits, conflicts and secret exclusion; owner-only listing and changes, audit, database checks and the next access token on migrated PostgreSQL; the trace level applied to the next agent turn; the model applied to the next AI request), 63 web unit and seven browser component tests, 29 end-to-end journeys (including Parâmetros on a 390 px phone: validation, save, persistence after reload, reset and history, without horizontal scrolling), smoke, builds, references and documentation. After a local database without the new migration let the API report ready while sign-in failed, identity and the agent now check operational_parameters at startup (regression test on migrated PostgreSQL), so an outdated schema fails explicitly as docs/setup.md requires. Review of 2026-10-08 (PR review comments): a parameter change and its parameter.updated audit event now commit in one database transaction (a failed audit undoes the change; tested on the in-memory store and on migrated PostgreSQL), and OPENAI_MODEL is validated against the ai.model identifier domain at startup. Remote CI passed on PR #6. Production values remain an owner review under PH-15.
